sections.skill: Tell debit, credit and payment processing apart

questions.prompt: Where does a business debit card take money from?

choices.text: A loan that must be repaid with interest

questions.intro: A business DEBIT card takes money straight from the business account. A business CREDIT card borrows money that must be repaid; unpaid balances usually charge interest. A PAYMENT PROCESSOR is a company that lets the business accept card or app payments from customers; it charges a fee, often a percentage plus a small fixed amount per sale, and deposits the rest into the business account, usually a day or more later. Know which tool moves money in, and which moves money out.

questions.prompt: A payment processor is which door?
questions.intro: Think of money moving through doors. A payment processor is an IN door: customers' card payments come through it into the business account, minus a fee. A debit card is an OUT door: money leaves the account immediately. A credit card is a borrowed OUT door: you spend now and must pay the card company back later, sometimes with interest.
